metadata.title: Spreadsheets on Demand
metadata.purpose: Teach viewers the three-tool workflow — Cowork to create, Google Sheets to host, ChatGPT extension to edit — so they can go from blank page to live spreadsheet without learning Excel.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro) — durations are word-count estimates until GATE 0 audio lock

beats.narration_text: Salam. This is Liam, in for Bear. What is the fastest way to build a spreadsheet from scratch with AI? Cowork creates it, Google Sheets hosts it, and ChatGPT edits it — here is the exact workflow.

props.ask: What is the best way to create a spreadsheet with AI?
props.answer_preview: The fastest path is Claude Cowork — it builds the actual file and...
props.command: What is the fastest way to build a spreadsheet from scratch with AI?

beats.narration_text: Claude Cowork is the best tool for creating spreadsheets — not editing them, creating them. Open the desktop app. Click the Cowork tab at the top. Connect Google Drive. Select your working folder. That is the setup.

card.sub: Cowork tab → connect Drive → select folder

beats.narration_text: The magic phrase in the prompt is: top ten assumptions to sanity check before execution. That single line keeps you in control. You are not just receiving output — you are approving the logic before Cowork builds the whole spreadsheet. That is the difference between a tool that helps you and one that runs away from you.

card.sub: Sanity-check phrase that keeps you in control of the logic

beats.narration_text: Once Cowork has built the spreadsheet, export it to Google Drive with one click. It opens directly in Google Sheets — no conversion, no reformatting. From there you can share it with anyone. If you want to keep editing with AI, stay in Cowork and follow up with more prompts. Or move to Google Sheets and bring in the ChatGPT extension.

illustration.concept: Three-stage workflow: Cowork → Google Sheets → ChatGPT extension
illustration.layout: Horizontal flow with three boxes connected by right-pointing arrows. Box 1: 'Cowork' (create from scratch). Box 2: 'Google Sheets' (host and share). Box 3: 'ChatGPT extension' (edit with AI). Below each box: a one-line action label. Terracotta arrows between boxes.

beats.narration_text: The ChatGPT extension inside Google Sheets is genuinely good for editing. You reference a tab or a cell range, write a plain-English instruction, and it adjusts the data. For example: change the bull scenario in Assumptions to be more optimistic, with realistic numbers. That kind of targeted edit works beautifully inside Sheets.

card.sub: ChatGPT extension in Google Sheets handles targeted cell edits

beats.narration_text: If spreadsheets are your full-time job, there is another tool worth knowing: Shortcut dot ai. It is built exclusively for spreadsheets and aims to replace both Microsoft and Google. It does not carry the same deep context that Cowork does, but it is a real alternative if you are building sheets all day.

card.sub: Spreadsheet-only AI tool — worth exploring if it's your whole job

beats.narration_text: Open Claude's desktop app right now. Go to the Cowork tab. Make sure Google Drive is connected. Start a new prompt with the sanity-check phrase: top ten assumptions before execution. Build your first spreadsheet. Then push it to Sheets and try the ChatGPT extension on one cell.

card.sub: Use the top-ten-assumptions phrase and export to Google Sheets

beats.narration_text: Cowork creates. Sheets hosts. ChatGPT edits. That three-tool workflow covers most of what anyone needs from a spreadsheet. No Excel formulas. No blank page. Just a prompt and a sanity check. This is Liam, in for Bear.

card.sub: this is Liam, in for Bear

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: you want to use Claude to work with spreadsheet data without copying and pasting every cell. Ask Claude to show you the three patterns for spreadsheet work: how to describe what you need in terms Claude can execute, how to structure the output so it pastes cleanly into Excel or Sheets, and what to do when the formula Claude gives you doesn't work in your version.
